<section class="mission-section">
  <div class="container">
    <div class="mission-content">
      <p class="mission-text">
        AffineDrift documents a research program that treats the golf swing as a nonlinear, control-affine system. We study how the passive dynamics of the golfer–club system (the drift) combine with deliberate muscular inputs to create repeatable trajectories. Every project connects rigorous mathematics with practical coaching intuition.
      </p>
      <ul class="mission-list">
        <li><strong>Drift diagnostics</strong>: quantify the state-dependent forces emerging from prior motion.</li>
        <li><strong>Control efficiency</strong>: map how torque channels and manipulability change through the swing.</li>
        <li><strong>Counterfactual analysis</strong>: simulate what happens when we alter inputs, constraints, or equipment.</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="mission-text">
        The site hosts full derivations, interactive tools, and replication notes so that other researchers can validate the work or extend it with their own data.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="theory-section">
  <div class="container">
    <h2>Why affine control matters</h2>
    <div class="theory-content">
      <div class="theory-intro">
        <p>
          A control-affine model separates the golf swing into a drift term \(f(x)\) that encodes passive dynamics and an input term \(g(x)u\) that captures muscular torques. This structure preserves nonlinear state dependence while keeping control inputs linear, which is exactly what we need to reason about coordination, manipulability, and causality.
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="coordination-section">
        <h3>Research focus</h3>
        <p>
          Our current work centers on three topics: (1) inverse dynamics interpretation with zero torque and zero velocity counterfactuals, (2) modal approximations for flexible shafts, and (3) how mechanical advantage migrates through impact. Each article documents the math and the computational workflow end-to-end.
        </p>
        <p>
          The <a href="articles/theory-part1.html">Drifter Manifesto</a> series walks through the derivation of the model. Later entries apply it to pendulum analogies, simulators, and experimental swing data.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
